items.title: Food festival hurt by LRT build in Mississauga will be compensated: mayoral candidate
items.summary: 6-billion Hurontario Street light-rail transit line has agreed to financially compensate organizers of a Mississauga food festival who complained their event last year was negatively impacted by construction delays, city councillor and mayoral candidate Dipika Damerla said this week. Damerla, one of four main candidates vying for Mississauga’s highest elected office, said during a Tuesday night mayoral debate that Metrolinx is going to provide compensation to the Cooksville Business Improvement Area, which stages the Taste of Cooksville outdoor festival each September. Participating alongside former mayor Bonnie Crombie and Ward 2 Coun. Alvin Tedjo in a debate hosted by the Canadian-Muslim Vote, Damerla said the City of Mississauga has done “a terrible job so far in holding Metrolinx to account” as it relates to updates on construction of the Hazel McCallion Line. In making the case that she could better deal with Metrolinx, Damerla said on Tuesday she pushed the provincial agency to pay the Cooksville BIA after its September 2025 Taste of Cooksville event was disrupted due to ongoing construction of the LRT line. She added festival organizers “couldn’t have the number of … stalls that they wanted because Metrolinx delayed some construction on Dundas (Street). ” Damerla argued at a September 2025 Mississauga city council meeting that Metrolinx should show “good faith” and reimburse Taste of Cooksville organizers. She added during the same meeting that the Cooksville BIA had sent a bill to Metrolinx for about $6,000. The invoice was sent because of “disruptions caused to the festival,” Damerla noted at the time.

items.title: A teacher at now-closed Holy Name of Mary in Mississauga has won a Prime Minister's Award for inspiring girls in STEM
items.summary: Karen Kozma, an Oakville resident now teaching at Pickering College in Newmarket, built an all-girls robotics team that became Holy Name of Mary’s largest club. Karen Kozma taught for 12 years at Holy Name of Mary College School in Mississauga, up to the school's closing after the 2025-26 school year. A high school teacher has earned one of Canada’s top honours in education for her work leading girls in STEM at a now-closed Mississauga high school. Karen Kozma, an Oakville resident, has been named a recipient of the Prime Minister’s Awards for Teaching Excellence in Science Technology Engineering and Math (STEM) achievement award. Beyond bringing her experience with a PhD. in electrical and computer engineering to grade 11 and 12 physics and computer science classes, the award recognizes her contributions beyond class time. In 2019, Kozma started an all-girls robotics team at Holy Name of Mary College School, which grew to be the school’s largest club. She was nominated for the Prime Minister’s Award by FIRST Robotics, which runs robotics competitions across Canada. Kozma, who taught for 12 years at the school and now teaches at Pickering College in Newmarket, said receiving the achievement award was “humbling” but it is really based on her students’ success. “It was never in my game plan to go for this award,” she said. “I was doing STEM in the classroom because I just love it.

items.title: Gun part seized in Mississauga leads to arrest in another part of Canada
items.summary: Police uncovered a stash of firearms, ammunition and other items on Canada’s East Coast following the seizure of a gun silencer at a mail processing facility in Mississauga. ” The gun part was destined for a Yarmouth residential address, the federal law enforcement agency said on Thursday. The CBSA in Mississauga then handed off the investigation to their colleagues in Halifax. As their investigation continued, CBSA officers, with help from members of the agency’s intelligence squad and the RCMP, executed a search warrant at the Yarmouth home on Feb. 25, 2026. “During the search of the residence, officers located and seized multiple unsecured firearms, as well as a homemade suppressor and many rounds of ammunition,” the Canada Border Services Agency said this week. A man was also arrested at the home, police added. The RCMP’s National Weapons Enforcement Support Team provided “expert analysis on the firearms and devices that were seized,” the CBSA said. Ian Pierre Surette, 25, of Yarmouth, Nova Scotia, faces 16 charges related to smuggling and various firearms-related offences, police said. The charges were laid on July 23.

items.title: Students in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon can apply for specialized high school programs
items.summary: Students preparing to enter high school have an opportunity to pursue specialized academic programs in Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon, with information nights starting later this month and applications opening in November. The Peel District School Board (PDSB) offers Regional Learning Choice Programs (RLCPs) at 17 secondary schools, giving students the chance to explore specific interests and academic pathways beyond the regular classroom experience. The programs cover a range of subjects, from science and technology to international business, the arts and skilled trades. Some focus on advanced academic study and university preparation, while others offer opportunities to develop creative abilities or practical technical skills. Unlike regular high school classes, which follow the Ontario curriculum across a broad range of subjects, these specialized programs build a particular area of interest into students’ learning experience. For example, students in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) programs can focus on those fields, while International Business and Technology (IBT) students combine business concepts with technology. Students in regional arts programs can pursue creative interests, while the Regional Skilled Trades program provides a more hands-on learning pathway. The board also offers Advanced Placement (AP) and International Baccalaureate (IB) programs, which provide academically challenging pathways designed to prepare students for post-secondary education. The programs are not intended to commit students to a single career at an early age. Instead, they give students opportunities to develop skills and explore subjects that may help guide their future education and career choices. Families interested in the programs can attend information nights hosted by participating secondary schools beginning Oct. 21.

items.title: Nominations for four Mississauga cycling awards are now open
items.summary: Know a cyclist or a cycling group in your community who has championed cycling or other active ways to move around the city? Nominate them for one of four awards today! Every year, the Mississauga Cycling Advisory Committee (MCAC) invites nominations for residents making a positive impact on cycling in Mississauga. The committee presents four awards that recognize people, businesses and students who help make cycling safer, more accessible and welcoming, while encouraging active transportation in the community. Nominations are now open for the Phil Green Recognition Award; the Cycling Equity, Diversity and Inclusion Recognition Award; the Business Recognition Award and the Youth/School Cycling Recognition Award. Presented to a person or a group who has made a strong effort to promote or enhance cycling or other forms of sustainable transportation in Mississauga throughout 2026. The award continues to honour Mississauga resident, Phil Green, who was a founding MCAC member and worked diligently to promote safe cycling in Mississauga. Presented to a person or persons who have demonstrated equity, diversity and inclusion while promoting cycling or other forms of sustainable transportation. , people with disabilities, low-income households) and other underrepresented communities in Mississauga. Presented to a business or business owner who has demonstrated exemplary effort to promote cycling to their employees and/or customers by breaking down barriers to cycling. This can include actions like providing safe bicycle parking or offering discounts for cyclists. Presented to a student or group of students who promoted cycling to their peers or actively set an example for safe cycling in Mississauga.

items.title: Driver in His 70s Hospitalized in Life-Threatening Condition After Medical Episode Causes Mississauga Rollover
items.summary: A vehicle flipped onto its side during a crash in Mississauga on Wednesday night. According to a Peel Regional Police spokesperson who spoke with Insauga.com, the driver, a man in his 70s, appeared to suffer a medical episode. Police say that medical episode is what caused the vehicle to crash and flip. The man was transported to a trauma centre in life-threatening condition, according to police. Insauga.com reports all roads affected by the crash have since reopened to traffic.

items.title: Crash in Mississauga leaves 1 person critically injured
items.summary: One person suffered life-threatening injuries after a crash in Mississauga. It happened on Network Road, near Highway 409, late Wednesday night. Paramedics said one person was trapped and later transported to hospital. The victim’s injuries are believed to be life-threatening.

items.title: No Candidate Has Claimed Any of the Nearly 1,900 Election Signs Mississauga Has Impounded So Far
items.summary: Mississauga.com reports city enforcement officers have impounded nearly 1,900 illegally placed election signs in less than two weeks, and so far no candidate has come forward to claim any of them. According to the outlet, the city told Mississauga News that staff removed 1,888 non-compliant signs between Sept. 27 and Oct. 9, a sharp jump from the roughly 1,300 signs reported impounded as of Oct. 5. The outlet says the city's senior communication advisor, Irene McCutcheon, noted that during the entire 2022 municipal election cycle enforcement officers impounded about 3,500 non-compliant signs in total. Mississauga.com reports candidates began putting up lawn signs on Sept. 27, and by Oct. 5 the city had received nearly 120 complaints from residents about illegal placements. According to the outlet, removed signs are stored in municipal work yards for a minimum of 30 days from the date they were taken down.

items.title: Toronto's New Emergency Backup Goalie Rule Gives Mississauga's Brendan Bonello Another Shot at the NHL
items.summary: Insauga.com profiles Brendan Bonello, a Mississauga product now serving as the Toronto Maple Leafs' emergency backup goaltender after the NHL moved to professionalize the role this season. According to the outlet, Bonello played junior and university hockey along with a brief stint in the ECHL before his playing career wound down, after which he began filling in at Leafs practices and game-day skates whenever an extra netminder was needed. The outlet reports the NHL now requires every team to carry an EBUG on its roster, with goaltenders wearing No. 00 who have 80 games or less of professional experience and haven't played under a standard NHL contract or suited up professionally in the past three seasons. Insauga.com quotes the 27-year-old Bonello, who grew up idolizing former Leafs netminder Ed Belfour, saying he doesn't take the second chance for granted. The outlet also cites Calgary's emergency backup Dusty Nickel, a 35-year-old former Junior A goalie who spent five seasons in the role before recently earning a permanent NHL contract.
